scene_translation: When you inserted the old key into the keyhole, the heavy door slowly opened. Inside, the room was dark, and the scent of incense drifted through the air. Opening the old notebook, you found a new message written in blue ink — 'Next, go to Suitengū. Before dusk.' At that moment, the voice of an elderly shrine priest came from behind you. 'Mr. Tesuto, I knew you would come here.'
grammar_note: 【〜ことは分かっておりました】This is keigo (formal/respectful speech) — the shrine priest uses おります, the humble form of います, as a mark of his formal register. Compare a young person who might say 「来るって分かってたよ」 — same meaning, completely different social register. When NPCs speak very formally to you, it often signals they are either respectful OR hiding something behind politeness.

mystery_memo: The back room at the shrine has been unlocked using the key from the locker — both items originated from the same source, suggesting the woman in blue planted them intentionally as a trail for the player. The notebook now contains a second message directing the player to Suitengū before dusk, escalating the time pressure. The elderly shrine priest (kannushi) knows the player's name without having been introduced, deepening the central mystery of who is orchestrating these events. The priest speaks in formal keigo, suggesting either genuine reverence or a careful, guarded manner — relationship status: unknown/watchful. The old tobacco shop grandfather (Scene 3) previously hinted at the shrine; his knowledge and the priest's awareness may be connected.
